g.text: The language shall specify a software design
as text: its high-level design, its
low-level design, the artefacts about it and
The language shall model the high-level
design as packages, the organisation above
A package shall be a box of the high-level
design: a black box that holds packages,

g.title: package app { package core { } } and package app@core { } are the same box; the flat form needs the outer package declared somewhere.
g.text: A package shall nest in a package, written
nested or reopened flat by its full path

g.title: @requirement and @constraint in the package or module body.
g.text: A package or a module shall realise

g.title: In the outermost package an artefact is of the system; in an inner package or a module, of that level. No keyword, no field.
g.text: The outermost package shall be the system,
and the level of an artefact shall follow
A package shall draw as a container of its

g.title: interface shell { kind: cli; operation buy(sku: string) -> int { exit 2: refused } }, at any level of packages. The kind and the fields of an operation are data, not grammar, so a new kind changes no syntax. Quality is a requirement or a constraint linked to the interface or to an operation. Replaces boundary (DS-54): an interface of the high level design is the external interface of a process, or of a library when it is binary.
g.text: A package shall declare the external
interfaces of what it builds, with their
The language shall model the low-level
design as modules of classes and their
A module shall be a namespace that reopens
across files and resolves names outward

g.title: No includes, no using; what already encloses you is omitted.
g.text: A bare name shall resolve from the innermost
scope outward, a qualified name across
modules, a pkg@ one across packages

g.title: A design declares what it designs and nothing else. A name read out of a type, a base, a template bound or a call that resolves to nothing the design declares is text: no relation, no expected node, no finding (std::string, Exception, subprocess::run). There is no extern module: a design that still writes one fails with E-SYNTAX until it is migrated.
g.text: A name the design does not declare shall be
text in a type, a base, a bound or a call,
A class shall be a type of the design:
class, dataclass or enum, with members

g.title: + # -, then abstract | static | const for methods, or owns | refs | shares and many | optional for attributes, then the name; a method named like its class is a constructor; name: type = default, the type as the code writes it. *args and **kwargs are parameter names like any other. Members are identified by name: an overload is one member.
g.text: A member shall carry visibility, modifiers,
a name, a type and an optional default

g.title: owns (default), refs, shares; many is *, optional 0..1, neither 1. A type is the code's text (std::map<std::string, Pool*>, list[Step], Pool | None): each name in it that the design declares is related with the attribute's ownership and multiplicity, or as a use from a parameter or a return; ds knows no container of any language. The one designed name of a type is what a call through it reaches. E-OWNERSHIP-CYCLE.
g.text: Ownership and multiplicity shall be written
on the attribute, and every name of its type
that the design declares shall be related;
parameters and returns shall give use

g.title: class Repository<T: Entity>; E-TEMPLATE-BOUND, never against an argument that is the user's own parameter (class Holder<T> : Base<T>). A base is written as the code writes it, IFormat<scene::SceneDocument> or Box[int]: its first name is what the class inherits and the whole text is kept; a method or a function takes parameters of its own, each<F>(f: F).
g.text: A template shall be identified by name and
arity and its arguments checked against
their bounds, and a base or a method shall
carry its template arguments as written

g.title: class Vector <<==, ordered, +, []>>; E-OPERATOR-UNDECLARED.
g.text: Operators shall be declared in the class
header as a set and refined in the body
Abstract and value shall be derived from the
Any entity or member shall open a body with
artefacts, and a member's body with rules
An enum shall be a value type with its
A sequence shall be the behaviour of a

g.title: sequence Class::method [/ scenario]; two declarations are a duplicate; the unnamed scenario is the default.
g.text: A sequence shall be identified by its
resolved subject and scenario, wherever it
The participants of a sequence shall be its
static context: self, the attributes, the
parameters, the locals written and the
A message shall name an operation of its
target's type and match its arity, inside
loop, alt and opt frames with prose

g.title: A call names a scenario as a declaration does, with a slash, and a scenario the operation does not declare is W-SCENARIO-UNDECLARED. Revision 2 adds the naming (DS-52): a trace could only go down through the default scenario.
g.text: A message to an operation with a behaviour
shall expand to its default scenario or to
the one it names, and coupling to another
A state machine shall be the behaviour of a

g.title: Idle -> Running on run [guard] / report; no nested states until a design asks for them.
g.text: The events and actions of a transition shall
be operations of the class, and the guard

g.title: REQ-00001-2: the revision is part of the identity; a link to a revision no longer declared is W-REVISION-DRIFT, resolved to the declared one.
g.text: An artefact shall be identified by its id

g.title: a requirement in a requirement refines it; a verification in a requirement verifies it; @refines, @requirement, @constraint elsewhere.
g.text: Nesting shall give the relation between

g.title: One-line forms for a requirement and a constraint; draft when no status.
g.text: An artefact shall carry title, text,
rationale, status and tags; a verification
its method and tests; a constraint its
A diagram shall be a selection of the model
that decides what to print and never what to
A diagram shall select by id, module or
package, with include and exclude, and print
A sequence diagram shall select a behaviour
as it is written and expand by depth
A requirement diagram shall show the
umbrella of an artefact: what refines,
The grammar shall read a specification as
The grammar shall ship highlight and fold
queries that name only nodes it defines

g.title: Files are read whole and are not units of meaning; a link nobody declares (an annotation, the subject of a behaviour) is an expected node reported once (W-REF-UNDECLARED) and never stops the load; a name in a type, a base, a bound or a call is text instead (REQ-00024-3); only syntax stops a file (E-SYNTAX).
g.text: A specification shall be a directory of .ds
files read as one, in any order

g.title: function name(params) -> type in a module, with a member's optional visibility in front, public when absent; two of one name are E-DUPLICATE-IDENTITY. A call to a function nobody designs is text (REQ-00024-3).
g.text: A function shall be an operation of a
module, outside any class, identified by its

g.title: Parameters and the return give use; the body holds notes, annotations, rules and nested artefacts.
g.text: A function shall carry a method's signature

g.title: sequence gather { }; there is no self. A call with no target is a function resolved outward from the module, `-> tasks::gather()` one of another module; a method reaches one its class does not declare. In a sequence diagram a function runs on its module's lifeline.
g.text: The behaviour of a function shall run on its
parameters and locals, and a call with no
target shall reach a function of the module
A class diagram shall draw each function as
a box of its own, stereotyped function

g.title: The result of a message has the type its operation returns. A call on a result is checked as a call on any other participant, and an argument against its parameter (W-ARG-TYPE): a value of a designed class must derive from the designed class the parameter names, and a literal, a number or a string, fits no designed class. A type the design does not declare (int, std::string, None) is the code's word, which ds does not read: it is never compared, and the result of any operation may be taken. A value whose type is not known, because its operation declares no return or does not resolve, has nothing to be checked against and gives no finding.
g.text: A value of a sequence shall have the type of
what produced it, and its uses shall be

g.title: return takes a name or a literal, never an expression. When the operation promises a designed class, a value of another class, or a literal, is reported (W-RETURN-TYPE); a return the design does not declare (void, int, None) is never compared. A name the context does not know is left alone, as an argument is. An operation that declares no return has nothing to check against.
g.text: A behaviour shall say what it gives back
with return, and that value shall be checked

g.title: sequence shell::buy / refused goes down through the scenario each call names. An operation with no sequence is W-OPERATION-NO-BEHAVIOUR, an outcome naming no scenario W-SCENARIO-UNDECLARED, and one whose trace ends in another value W-OUTCOME-MISMATCH. What cannot be told, a value that is not a literal at the end of the trace, gives no finding.
g.text: An operation of an interface shall have a
sequence, and each outcome it promises shall
name a scenario whose trace ends in that

g.title: state web { view Home { text: ... } Home -> Done on buy }. A view holds free text and the requirements and constraints that bind it, nothing that reinvents HTML. An event that names an operation goes down to it; any other is a label. W-VIEW-UNDECLARED, W-VIEW-UNREACHABLE and W-VIEW-NO-WAY-OUT. Views are optional: a bare machine asks nothing.
g.text: The state machine of an interface shall be
its navigation, with views as its states,
and shall report the views with no way in or
A state diagram shall draw the states and
the jumps of a machine, and of an interface
its navigation with what each view shows

g.title: One rule at every level: a box connects to another through a public child. A package's public children are its interfaces and modules, a module's its classes and functions, a class's its methods and attributes. A child is public unless it says -, and is seen from inside its parent, so siblings see each other. A member that says # is protected: seen from inside its class and from a class that derives from it (DS-224). A call or a type that crosses anything private or protected on its way down is W-NOT-VISIBLE; a public member showing a private type is W-PRIVATE-LEAK.
g.text: Any child of a box may be private, and
nothing outside its parent shall reach it

g.title: open: shop@store@stock opens that box and the way to it; open: written alone closes every other box, and open: with nothing after it closes them all; a diagram that writes no cut draws everything open. An edge that loses an end to a closed box is lifted to it, and what stays inside a closed box is not drawn. A behaviour that crosses boxes counts too, so an interface reaches what handles it though no type says so. The component view is derived, never written. Revision 3 (DS-229): open: is one of the ways a cut is written (REQ-00126-1, REQ-00127-1, REQ-00128-1); alone it means what it meant. Revision 4 (DS-230): a lifted edge no longer says only that one box depends on the other; it is a structural bond or a use (REQ-00137-1). Revision 5 (DS-244): a closed box lists what it offers as a class lists its members, a compartment for each kind of thing in one order (packages, modules, interfaces, classes, dataclasses, enums, functions), each by name and each marked with the badge a box of its own would carry.
g.text: A class diagram shall open the boxes it
names and close the rest, each closed box

g.title: opt <prose> / refused { ... return 2 } names a branch; a bare return ends it. The path of a scenario takes what is shared and its own branch, up to the return that ends it; the default path takes no named branch; of an alt with one named side, the other side is taken; a branch it cannot tell is kept as a frame. A call, a diagram and an exit code ask for the path by its name, as they do for a sequence of its own, which stays for paths that share nothing. A name given twice is W-SCENARIO-TWICE. A behaviour asked for by its subject is drawn whole, its early returns included; an unnamed call follows the default path.
g.text: A branch of a sequence shall name a
scenario, a path through that one behaviour,
so what scenarios share is written once

g.title: Each kind names the fields it carries, each with a type (text, name, names, type, params, number, status, patterns) and who sets it (the author, the syntax, or the checker), the flags it takes and the kinds it may be declared inside; a field whose name ends in * is a family (local.*, exit *, contract.*). Each relation names the kinds it may go from and to. Everything the binder and the checker put in a model is something the metamodel declares.
g.text: The language shall be declared once as a
metamodel: every kind with its fields, flags
and parents, every relation with the kinds

g.title: A key: value an entity carries that the metamodel does not declare for its kind (a typo, or a field the language does not know) is a warning at the entity, naming the field and the kind. It is kept in the model: the warning does not drop it.
g.text: A field that its kind does not declare shall

g.title: usecase UC-00001-1 greet(name: string) -> Greeting { outcome default: ...; outcome empty-name -> none: ... } is an artefact identified by its id with its revision: a title, a status, the requirements that bind it (@requirement), an optional signature and its outcomes, default the ending that goes well and every other one a scenario. It names no interface: an interface operation realises it (operation greet(...) : UC-00001-1), whoever drives that interface. A specific use case specialises a generic one after a colon and keeps its signature, its outcomes and its requirements. A design without use cases owes none.
g.text: A use case shall be declared as a contract
with its outcomes, realised by interface
operations and specialised by a specific use

g.title: An operation that takes or gives something else than the use case it realises, or a specific use case that does so against its generic, is W-USECASE-SIGNATURE. An outcome, its own or inherited, that the operation handles with no scenario is W-USECASE-OUTCOME-UNHANDLED; a scenario the operation handles that no outcome names is W-SCENARIO-NO-OUTCOME. A use case no operation realises, directly or through one that specialises it, is W-USECASE-UNREALISED; a realisation or a specialisation of an id that is no use case is W-USECASE-UNDECLARED.
g.text: The check shall hold every operation that
realises a use case to its contract, outcome

g.title: language: cpp in a package or a module; cpp, c, python, typescript or lua, the languages argos reads. What a box holds is written in its language unless it says another, and the check fills the language down, so every package and module of the model carries it. One ds does not know, or two at once (a reopened box that says two), is W-LANGUAGE-UNKNOWN. A box that says nothing and is held by nothing that says has no language.
g.text: A package or a module shall say what its
code is written in, and what it holds shall
be written in the same unless it says

g.title: @consumes sistema@broker@publish in a box binds a consumes relation from the box to the interface; the box that offers the interface is the provider. Like every annotation it binds the same written in the box or in an extension block anywhere else, so the wiring of a system can live in a file of its own (as design/wiring.ds does for requirements) and a design brought in whole can be connected from above without being touched. What an annotation means is read from the metamodel's table of annotations, declared once.
g.text: A package, a module or a class shall declare
that it uses an interface another box
offers, in its own body or from another file

g.title: interface port { ... } inside module face is p@face::port, offered by the module. A behaviour reaches an interface's operation as it reaches a method: local ds: p@engine then -> ds.check(text), or a parameter or an attribute typed by the interface; the call names the operation, so the consumer depends on the contract and not on the class that realises it. In the viewer a module's interfaces come first inside it.
g.text: A module shall offer interfaces like a
package, and a behaviour shall call an
interface's operation through a local, a
parameter or an attribute typed by it

g.title: A call to an operation of an interface another box offers needs a @consumes of that interface on the caller or on a box it lives in, written there or in a wiring file (W-CONSUMES-UNDECLARED). A @consumes that none of the box's behaviours calls is dead, said only once the box has behaviours (W-CONSUMES-UNUSED). A call to a method of a class that realises an interface, from outside the class's module, goes around the contract when the method answers an operation of that interface (W-CONSUMES-BYPASS); a method the interface does not offer cannot be called through it and is no bypass (DS-106). An interface's own sequences realise it, and a box calling an interface it offers depends on nothing.
g.text: The checker shall compare what a box
declares it uses with what its behaviours
call, and report what is not declared, what
is declared and never called, and a call

g.title: rule <name> { @requirement <ID>; for <kind> <variable> [in <box>], ...; where <literals>; holds <literals> | never <literals> } in a package, a module, a class or a member; definition <name>(<parameters>) { if <literals> ... } names a relation derived from others, one case per if line. A literal is a relation of the metamodel (c uses x), a kind (x is class), containment (x in p@core), a comparison (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=) of entities or values, a definition applied (reaches(c, x)) or the literal argument of a call (arg(k, msg, v)), negated by not; a bare name is a variable, an entity is written qualified and a value is a number or a string. What a rule says is read from this syntax and never from prose: holds: <words> does not parse. A rule is a design piece with a name, not an artefact with a revision: it makes a requirement real in a narrower context and may name the entities of the design, which a requirement does not. A rule that answers to no requirement, or says no claim or more than one, and a definition with no case, are findings.
g.text: The language shall declare rules and
definitions in the box they apply to, in a
formal syntax: what they speak about, which
of them, and what holds, answering to a

g.title: Rules are evaluated as Datalog with stratified negation over the model: the facts are the declared entities with their kinds, every relation of the metamodel and containment at any depth. A definition is computed to its fixpoint, recursion included; a rule's holds is broken by each binding of its ranges and where that has no answer, its never by each binding that has one, reported with the binding and the answer (E-RULE-BROKEN). The model is finite, so every rule is decided. A formula that names an unknown kind, relation, entity or definition (E-RULE-UNKNOWN), applies a definition to the wrong number of arguments (E-RULE-ARITY), tests a variable no positive literal binds (E-RULE-UNSAFE) or negates a definition through its own recursion (E-RULE-UNSTRATIFIED) is reported and not evaluated.
g.text: The checker shall decide every structural
rule over the model and report each binding
of its ranges that breaks it

g.title: A call of a sequence is a message entity that calls an operation; arg(k, p, v) holds when the call k passes to the parameter p of what it calls a value v written as a literal in the sequence, a number or a string. Values compare numbers as numbers and anything else as written. A call that passes a name instead of a literal has no arg fact for that parameter, so a rule that asks for one in its where leaves it out: undecided in the design, it is neither kept nor broken. A broken rule is reported at the first thing it ranges over, the call in its sequence.
g.text: The checker shall decide the rules over the
calls of the sequences against the literal
arguments they pass, and report each call
that breaks one where the call is written

g.title: Each breach the evaluator finds is kept by the rule's identity: the variables of its ranges and where as bound, for a never the answer that breaks it, and the location of the first thing the rule ranges over. All of them are kept, although the findings stop at a few per rule. The JSON export carries them under breaches, and the Python package loads them as Model.breaches, so a reader lights what breaks a rule without reading the findings' prose.
g.text: The engine shall keep every binding that
breaks a rule, with its answer and where it
lands, and hand it structured to the export

g.title: A method named ~ and the class's name is its destructor (flag destructor). It is no part of the contract: like a constructor, it does not count against the derived interface stereotype, so an interface declares the virtual destructor the C++ guide asks of it.
g.text: A class shall declare its destructor as
~Name(), and an interface may have one

g.title: `-> diff::Diff::compare(a, b)`: a message with no participant whose qualified name names an operation of a class calls it on the class itself, as `-> tasks::gather(x)` calls a function of another module. The operation must be static; one that is not is W-MSG-NOT-STATIC, since it needs an instance: a local, an attribute or a parameter.
g.text: A message shall call a class's static
operation by its qualified name, with no

g.title: A state named in the transitions that the walk from the initial state never enters is W-STATE-UNREACHABLE: a state left over, or a transition missing. The initial state is the one written, or the one the machine starts in when it is not written (REQ-00143-1). A machine with neither says nothing, since where it starts cannot be told. The navigation of an interface has its own (W-VIEW-UNREACHABLE).
g.text: The checker shall report a state of a
class's machine that no transition leads to

g.title: fail ParseError ends a path where a return would go, with the failure's name as text, as a type is written. attempt { ... } on IoError / unreadable { ... } runs its steps and handles what they fail with, one on each: a handler that fails with another translates the failure, one that returns resolves it, and a failure no handler names goes on to the caller. The default path does not fail: it takes the attempt's steps and no handler; a handler that names a scenario is the path of that failure. The diagram draws the failure and each handler.
g.text: A sequence shall say where a path ends
failing and where a failure of what it calls

g.title: A failure starts where a path ends failing and goes up to every caller that does not handle it: an attempt handles, around the steps it runs, what its handlers name; a handler's own steps are not handled by its attempt. Computed until nothing changes, so calls that call each other end. Each operation carries escapes, the failures, and escape.<failure>, the operations it comes up through and the behaviour (or the scenario of one) that starts it. A call ds cannot follow, to an operation with no behaviour, is taken not to fail. ds query <workspace> failures <operation> answers each escaping failure, named by the operation it starts in.
g.text: The checker shall compute what failures
escape each operation, with the path each
comes up by, and the query shall answer it

g.title: + load(path: string) -> Book fails LoadError, ParseError promises what may escape; fails nothing promises none. What escapes and the signature does not say is W-FAILURE-UNDECLARED; what it says and no path of its behaviour fails with is W-FAILURE-UNREACHED. An interface operation is a boundary: what escapes it is said in its signature, or nothing may. Any other operation is held to its signature only when it writes one. An operation with no behaviour fails as its signature says, so a call into a library can be said to fail.
g.text: A signature shall say what an operation may
fail with, and the checker shall hold it to
what escapes, and a boundary to saying it

g.title: A @word outside the table of annotations is a warning where it is written, naming the word and the words the language knows. The link it makes is kept (refers): the warning does not drop it, and loading never fails on it.
g.text: An annotation word the language gives no
meaning to shall be reported as

g.title: The metamodel names the values of its closed fields: status (draft, approved, obsolete), a verification's method and level, a diagram's kind. Any other value is a warning at the entity, naming the field, the value and the values it takes; an empty value is left alone. The value is kept in the model. Revision 2 (DS-231): a diagram has no level any more; the cut is written with close: (REQ-00126-1).
g.text: A closed field carrying a value it does not
take shall be reported as W-FIELD-VALUE

g.title: include, exclude and open take an identity, a prefix with * over the identity or the scope (p@m::* is the module p@m and everything in it), a module named as such, or a template written without its arity, read alike by class, sequence, state and requirement diagrams. A pattern that names nothing the workspace declares is a warning at the diagram. A pattern over a box that exists and is empty is not: a level with no children is valid.
g.text: A diagram pattern shall read the same in
every kind of diagram, and one that names
what nothing declares shall be reported as

g.title: The kind of a variable is read from its range or from a positive kind literal, and the kind of an entity from the model. When a relation literal binds its source to a kind the relation never leaves, or its target to a kind it never reaches, by the metamodel, the literal matches nothing: the rule is decided by vacuity. It is a warning at the literal; the rule is still evaluated.
g.text: A relation literal that binds an end to a
kind the relation never joins there shall be

g.title: Requirements that refine each other through any chain are E-REFINES-CYCLE; classes or use cases that derive from each other are E-INHERITANCE-CYCLE; each cycle is said once. A requirement whose refined requirement is written inside its own box, further down the containment axis, is a warning: the detail stands above what it details. The axis is read from where each is written, never from the prefix of its id.
g.text: A cycle of refines or of inherits shall be
an error, and a requirement that refines one
written inside its own box shall be reported

g.title: When a class realises an interface (@interface) and declares, or inherits, a method named like one of the interface's operations, their parameters and returns are compared as the idea each type commits to: qualifiers and spaces dropped, the rest as the code writes it. A difference is a warning at the method. An operation the class does not declare is no finding: that is absence.
g.text: A method that answers an operation of an
interface its class realises shall take and
give what the operation does, or be reported

g.title: A package below the system or a module that a pattern takes is drawn as a box, with or without children, and an entity is drawn inside the box its scope names, a package scope included: an interface declared in a package sits in that package. Nothing below a box is needed to see the box.
g.text: A class diagram shall draw every box it

g.title: What a sequence uses or couples to is drawn from its subject's box (a method's class, a function, an operation's interface), not from the module it is written in. Behaviour that crosses boxes is drawn whether or not the diagram writes open:, so a diagram that does not write open: draws what one that opens every box draws; a coupling an edge between the two already says gives no second arrow. A box's @consumes of an interface is drawn as a dependency, before any behaviour confirms it.
g.text: A class diagram shall draw a behaviour's
behaviour with or without open, and draw a

g.title: Every source of satisfies and constrained-by is drawn under the artefact: a package, a module, an interface, a class, an enum, a function, a use case, a rule. A method, an attribute, an operator or an operation answers through the class or the interface that holds it, and a holder and its member that answer the same artefact draw one edge.
g.text: A requirement diagram shall draw whatever
answers to a requirement, a member through
the class or interface that holds it

g.title: The failures the steps of an attempt can raise are those its messages fail with and those that escape the operations they call. A handler that names none of them handles nothing. Said only when every operation called in the attempt says how it fails, by a behaviour or by a signature; a call that says nothing leaves the handler alone.
g.text: A handler of a failure that no step of its
attempt can fail with shall be reported as

g.title: Six codes say that something is not yet written: an interface operation with no sequence (W-OPERATION-NO-BEHAVIOUR), an outcome with no scenario (W-USECASE-OUTCOME-UNHANDLED), a use case nothing realises (W-USECASE-UNREALISED), an approved requirement nothing verifies (W-REQ-NO-VERIFICATION), a verification by test with no tests (W-VER-NO-TEST), a rule that answers to no requirement (W-RULE-NO-REQUIREMENT). They are of severity coverage: ds check does not report or count them, the check's JSON and the export carry them apart, and ds query <workspace> coverage [identity] lists them. An oracle corpus marks them with // ? as it marks a finding with // !.
g.text: What is not yet written shall be no finding,
kept apart as coverage and answered when

g.title: A requirement nested in a class, a member, a function or another design entity binds requires from the entity, and a nested constraint binds constrained-by, as @requirement and @constraint do: two syntaxes that only change where the artefact is filed. Every kind that may nest an artefact, an attribute and an operator among them, may carry either annotation, and satisfies and constrained-by leave the same kinds, a state machine included. In a package or a module a nested artefact still gives its level.
g.text: Nesting an artefact in a design entity shall
say what annotating it says, and whatever
may nest an artefact may annotate it

g.title: close: shop@warehouse closes that box; close: shop@sales@* every box that begins so; close: module every module wherever it is, and close: package every package below the outermost one, so a cut runs at one kind of box without counting levels. What a closed box holds is lifted to it, as with open:. The outermost package is the drawing itself and never closes. The drawing and ds query shows read the same cut. A pattern that names no box is W-DIAGRAM-UNDECLARED; a kind names no box and is none.
g.text: A diagram shall close the boxes close:
names, by name, by prefix or by kind, and

g.title: With both written, close: draws the line and open: goes through it: close: module with open: shop@sales@till closes every module but the till. One rule for the two fields, with no order between patterns to learn. open: written alone keeps its meaning (REQ-00064-3).
g.text: A box that open: names shall stay open, with
the way to it, whatever close: closes

g.title: cut: HLD_Till takes the open: and close: of that diagram, and what the diagram writes itself is added to them, so several drawings share one cut written once. A diagram named that nothing declares is W-DIAGRAM-UNDECLARED, and the diagram is drawn with what it writes itself. Diagrams that take each other's cut are read once each.
g.text: A diagram shall take the cut of the diagram
cut: names and add what it writes itself

g.title: The open:, close: and cut: of a class diagram mean the same in a sequence diagram. Every participant is drawn as what stands for it on the cut: a closed box is one lifeline for everything inside it, and what no closed box holds keeps a lifeline of its own. A message whose two ends have the same representative is internal and is not drawn; one that crosses is drawn between the representatives, and into a closed box it says which of its children takes it (Desk::sell). A frame of the detail is kept around what crosses inside it, and one in which nothing crosses is not drawn. ds query shows answers the same participants. It replaces level: module, which lifted to one fixed rung, drew only the direct calls and ignored depth; a diagram that still writes it is told so (W-FIELD-UNKNOWN).
g.text: A sequence diagram shall stand on the cut
the diagram writes: one lifeline for each
closed box, and the messages that cross from

g.title: The calls have a cut of their own, written like the cut of the boxes. fold: names the calls that are not followed (* for every call, a box for every call that lands in it, an operation), and every other call is followed. unfold: names the calls that are followed, whatever fold: says; written alone it folds every other call, and with nothing after it the diagram draws only what the behaviour itself writes. depth: n is the uniform case for the calls neither names. With none of the three, a diagram that writes a cut follows every call, since what a closed box does inside is seen only through what crosses out of it, and a diagram that writes no cut follows none, as before. A pattern that names nothing is W-DIAGRAM-UNDECLARED.
g.text: A sequence diagram shall follow the calls
that unfold:, fold: and depth: say, and
every call when it stands on a cut and they

g.title: With close: module, a requirement a class answers to is drawn realised by the module that holds the class, once. The artefacts themselves are never lifted. ds query shows answers the same boxes.
g.text: A requirement diagram shall draw what
answers to a requirement as the box that
stands for it on the cut the diagram writes

g.title: sequence UC-00001-1 { } is a scenario of the use case, and sequence UC-00001-1 / sold-out another; sequence sales { } is what a box does. Its names resolve from the scope the use case is declared in, or from inside the box. In a scenario of a use case a message with nobody written before its arrow is sent by whoever asks for the use case, from outside the design; in one of a box, by the box. A level written alone is a complete design: nothing below it has to exist.
g.text: A sequence shall be the behaviour of a use
case, a package or a module as well: a

g.title: sales in shell -> sales.sell(item) is the package shop@sales, resolved like any name, from the innermost scope outward; no local declares it. A value of the static context of that name comes first (REQ-00036-2). A name that is neither, the sender's included, is text, and its message is not checked (REQ-00024-3). In a drawing a box that is named is one lifeline, the same one a closed box has on a cut (REQ-00129-1), and ds query shows answers it.
g.text: A participant of a sequence shall be
nameable as what it is: a package, a module,
an interface or a class the behaviour sees

g.title: sales -> warehouse.take(item) leaves the sales. The sender is who calls: what it may see (W-NOT-VISIBLE) and what it declares to use (W-CONSUMES-UNDECLARED) are checked from it, and it is where the message leaves in a drawing. A message with no sender written is the subject's, as before.
g.text: A message shall be sent by the participant
written before its arrow, and by the subject
of the behaviour when none is written

g.title: A package offers the operations of its interfaces, a module its functions. Bound, the message is a call like any other: its arguments are checked (E-MSG-ARITY, W-ARG-TYPE), it expands to the behaviour of the operation, one step below, and the box stays the participant. With no operation of that name, or with more than one, the message is a label: the level below is not written yet, which is W-MESSAGE-NO-OPERATION in the coverage (REQ-00124-1) and never a finding. A message to an interface or a class that lacks the operation is still W-MSG-UNDECLARED: what is written is written.
g.text: A message to a box shall be bound to the
operation the box offers under that name,
and be kept as a label, listed as coverage,

g.title: The level below a scenario of a use case is the behaviour of the operation it is asked through: a message nobody sends, bound to an operation that has a behaviour (the scenario of the same name, when the operation has one). That behaviour is unfolded and lifted onto the participants of the scenario: whatever one of them holds, it stands for. The crossings the scenario writes have to be found among those of the level below, in order: a message bound to an operation finds a call of that operation, a label a crossing between the same two. The higher level may leave crossings out. One it writes that the level below never makes, or makes fewer times, is W-LEVEL-NO-CROSSING; one made at another place is W-LEVEL-ORDER. Both need the sender to be all written below: something is seen to happen in it, and every call made in it has a behaviour. Otherwise what the sender does is not known yet and the crossing is W-LEVEL-NOT-BELOW in the coverage (REQ-00124-1), which says which steps of the high level have their detail beneath. A scenario with no behaviour below it is held to nothing.
g.text: The scenario of a use case and the behaviour
below it shall agree on what crosses between
the participants of the scenario, and in

g.title: Between classes a relation keeps its own kind: composition, aggregation, inheritance, realisation, use. When an end of it is lost to a closed box it is lifted, and between boxes it is one of two things. A structural bond: one owns, refers to, derives from or realises something of the other; drawn as a solid arrow. A use: it names a type of the other, calls it, sends it a message or declares its use; drawn as a dashed arrow. Each is drawn once between two boxes, however many relations of the detail make it, and what stays inside a closed box is not drawn. With the boxes open nothing changes.
g.text: A relation lifted onto a closed box shall
read as one of two bonds, structural or
uses, with one arrow of each at most between

g.title: sales -> warehouse.take(item) gives the relation sends from the sales to the warehouse, once, however many messages say it. The sender is the participant written before the arrow, or the box a scenario is of; whoever asks for a use case is outside the design and gives none. Between boxes it is a use (REQ-00137-1), so a design that has only its high level draws its boxes connected by what its scenarios say.
g.text: A message written between two participants
shall say that the sender uses the receiver

g.title: diagram TOUR_Buy { kind: tour; include: shop@shell::buy; close: module } takes the fields of a sequence diagram: the behaviour it follows, the cut, and the calls it follows. It is one drawing of two parts. The sequence, as a sequence diagram of the same fields draws it. And who takes part, drawn as boxes: each lifeline of the sequence is one box of the other part, whether the cut closes it or a scenario written between boxes names it, with the relations between them lifted (REQ-00137-1) and the boxes around them as open context. The parts are drawn side by side, and one under the other where the width asked for does not hold them, or in a terminal. ds query shows answers who takes part.
g.text: A tour shall draw, in one diagram and on one
cut, the boxes that take part in a behaviour

g.title: Paid if status = Paid, not cancelled. A state is computed, not kept: its rule says when the subject of the machine is in it, over what the subject holds. The literals are joined by commas and all hold. A literal is an attribute compared with a value (=, !=), or a name alone: a boolean attribute, or a condition with a name when the subject holds nothing so called; `not` turns a literal round. A state may have several rules, each one way of being in it. The jumps are written beside the rules as they always were (REQ-00040-1), and a state with no rule is a name, as before.
g.text: A state of a machine shall be written with
the rule that computes it over what its

g.title: The rules of a machine exclude each other, so that whatever its subject holds it is in one state. Two rules of different states that some context satisfies together are W-STATE-OVERLAP, and the finding says one such context: Lamps can be Left and Both at once: when hazard = true, lever = Left. It is read from the rules alone: two rules exclude each other when they ask one name for values that cannot both be. Two rules of one state may hold together. What no rule covers is nothing to report: a machine that says less is complete.
g.text: The checker shall report two states of a
machine that can hold at once, with a

g.title: A comparison with a value the type of the attribute does not have is W-STATE-VALUE, and it says the values the type has. A comparison of something the subject does not hold is W-STATE-UNDECLARED. A rule whose literals exclude each other is W-STATE-IMPOSSIBLE: the subject can never be in that state. A rule reported so is said once and is not held to the others. An attribute whose values cannot be listed (a number, a text) is compared as written.
g.text: The checker shall report a rule of a state
that cannot hold as it is written

g.title: The start of a machine whose states have rules is derived: the state in which the defaults of the attributes its rules read are. A start that is written is the start. Defaults that are in no state, and an attribute with no default, give no start.
g.text: A machine shall start in the state the
defaults of its subject are in, when its

g.title: A state a rule computes shows its rule under its name, one line for each rule it has, and is drawn though no jump names it. The arrow from the start goes to the state the machine starts in (REQ-00143-1).
g.text: A state diagram shall draw each state with

g.title: The behaviours written are read as they are, and nothing is asked of them. Along a behaviour, what it calls an event on may be in any state to begin with; a call of an event moves it by the jumps on that event, and a jump with a guard may leave it where it was. A frame may not happen: what comes after it finds the receiver as the frame leaves it or as it was; the sides of an alt are each one way, and a loop is read once, since its receiver may be another each time. An operation that is no event of the machine moves nothing. A call the machine lets happen from none of the states its receiver may be in is W-STATE-ORDER, where the call is made: Desk::rush calls order.cancel() when order can only be Shipped: the machine of Order lets cancel happen from Open or Paid.
g.text: The checker shall report a call of an event
that the machine of its receiver lets happen
from no state the receiver may be in

g.title: The jump keeps its label as it is written, and says besides the behaviours written that call its event: pay is called in Desk::rush, Desk::sell. A jump whose event no behaviour calls says nothing more.
g.text: A state diagram shall say, on each jump, the

g.title: diagram TB_Order { kind: table; include: shop@order::Order }. The events and the states are in the order the machine writes them. A cell says the state the jumps on the event lead to from the state above it, with the guard of a jump that has one and every jump when there are several; where the machine has no jump the cell is empty. It is drawn as SVG and as terminal text, like every diagram.
g.text: A table diagram shall draw a machine as a
table: its events down, its states across,
and in each cell where the event takes the

g.title: The heading of a row says the behaviours written that call its event. A call the machine lets happen from no state its receiver may be in (REQ-00145-1) is said in the cell of each of those states, with the behaviour that makes it: the place in the table where the behaviours and the machine disagree.
g.text: A table diagram shall say who calls each
event, and the cell in which a behaviour

g.title: diagram TB { kind: table; for <kind> <variable> [in <box>], ...; where <literals>; column <name>: <what> ... }. The rows are said as a rule says what it speaks about: every binding of the ranges that passes the filter. A column is a field of the row (r.title; name and id are what every entity has, holds says of a rule whether the model keeps it), what is related to the row (x where r satisfies x: every x that answers, by its name), or a yes or no (holds <literals>). The first column heads each row. A comparison reads a field of what a variable is bound to (r.status = "draft"), in a table and in a rule alike, and an artefact is in the box it is written in. A table written this way is the model's answer, kept when the design is checked; one that names a machine is REQ-00147-2. A cell too long for one line goes on several.
g.text: A table diagram shall list what its ranges
and its filter answer, a row each, with a
cell under each column it writes

g.title: What a box consumes, uses or calls of an interface of another box is said by the use drawn between the two, lifted or written between them as they are: a line per interface, its name and the operations asked of it. A use that goes through no interface says nothing, and a structural bond never does. The drawing carries it as what the arrow says when pointed at.
g.text: A use drawn between two boxes shall say the
interfaces of the one it reaches that the
other goes through, with the operations

g.title: A state machine is its subject's identity with ::state, and a sequence its subject's with ::sequence; a member written with that name takes the identity of the behaviour when the behaviour is written too. The member is reported where it is written, once, and the behaviour keeps the identity whichever of the two is written first, with nothing else said of the collision. A member named state or sequence whose holder has no such behaviour is an ordinary member.
g.text: A member named after a behaviour its holder
has shall be E-NAME-RESERVED, and the

g.title: A requirement written in a box has that box as its home. A box, interface, class, function or member that answers to it from outside that box is a warning: the requirement is written at one place and realised outside it. The finding names the innermost box around the home that holds every piece realising the requirement: where the requirement would stand with all of them inside. What holds a piece is read from where it is written, never from the prefix of its id. A requirement written at the root holds everything, and a requirement nothing realises is no finding. A system that adopts the requirement of another, written in a package of its own that no box shares with it (a library's), answers to it as to any artefact: no finding either.
g.text: A piece that answers to a requirement whose
home does not hold it shall be reported as
that holds the home and every piece that

g.title: After the scopes, from the innermost outward, a bare name (no :: and no @) is looked for among the classes and enums of the package it is written in, at any depth of its modules: the one of that name and arity is it, and another package is never asked. When two or more share it, it relates nothing and W-NAME-AMBIGUOUS is reported once where it is written, naming every candidate by its identity. A name written from the top package, a name nobody declares and a template parameter say nothing. It is the rule argos applies to the code, so Plan, written as a Python module imports it from a sibling module, finds the class there.
g.text: A bare name that no scope declares shall
resolve to the one class of that name in its
package, and warn when two share it

g.title: An attribute has one ownership (owns, refs, shares) and one multiplicity (many, optional). Two of either kind, or one written twice, say two things at once: an error at the attribute, which keeps the first one written.
g.text: An attribute written with two ownerships or
two multiplicities shall be reported as

g.title: A node binder takes the kinds of node of one construct and binds one of them. The binder reaches every one through INodeBinder, by the table, and what several constructs share is a part each is given by reference. A construct added to the language is a binder added beside the others, which do not change.
g.text: The binder shall bind each construct of the
language through a binder of its own,

g.title: A node binder and a part declare, relate, annotate and note through the context they are given, which holds the model, the notes and where the node is written. What binds a file holds no model of its own.
g.text: Every binder shall write into the model

g.title: What binds a construct is its node binder's, what several share is a part's, what reads the tree is the reader's and what reads a type's text is the token's. A function of the module would be a responsibility no class names.
g.text: Every operation of the binder shall be a
member of the class whose responsibility it

g.title: The kinds, the relations, the codes, the annotations and how each kind is written are built by the metamodel's own builders when it is made, once where the engine starts, and read from then on through its questions. What builds them belongs to the metamodel and nothing outside the model calls it.
g.text: The metamodel shall build its own tables

g.title: What splits, joins, trims and escapes text takes text and gives text. It reads no model, no tree and no document, so every module of the engine can use it and it uses none of them.
g.text: The text module shall depend on no other

g.title: Each function of text answers from what it is given: no attribute of the module keeps anything between two calls, so a call reads the same in any order and from any module.
g.text: The text module shall hold no state

g.title: What a cut is, what stands for an id on it, how a box is lifted and how a relation reads once lifted are the Cut's. A function of the module would be a responsibility no class names.
g.text: Every operation of the axis shall be a
member of the class whose responsibility it

g.title: A cut is computed from what the model keeps and the diagram writes, and read by the query, the drawing and the check alike. The axis asks the model its questions and calls none of what changes it.
g.text: The axis shall read the model it cuts and

g.title: Facts reads the model once into what a rule is evaluated over: the declared entities of each kind, every relation both ways, the names a formula writes resolved, and what each definition holds for; it is the pieces' one reader of the model. RuleValidator checks each formula before it is evaluated, Strata orders the definitions, and Solver answers a body over the facts alone. Evaluator directs them: it records into the facts what the validator resolved and what the definitions derive, and writes the breaches and the tables into the model.
g.text: The evaluator shall direct four pieces, and
the solver shall read the facts and never
